+ //! Hardware Abstraction Layer
+ //! 
+ //! This module contains all hardware-related functionality including:
+ //! - GPIO operations
+ //! - SysTick timer
+ //! - UART communication
+ //! - Button handling
+ //! - Traffic light control
+ 
+ use core::ptr::{read_volatile, write_volatile};
+ use cortex_m::asm;
+ 
+ // =============================================================================
+ // GPIO FUNCTIONALITY
+ // =============================================================================
+ 
+ pub const MODER: u32 = 0x00;
+ pub const OTYPER: u32 = 0x04;
+ pub const OSPEEDR: u32 = 0x08;
+ pub const PUPDR: u32 = 0x0C;
+ pub const IDR: u32 = 0x10;
+ pub const BSRR: u32 = 0x18;
+ 
+ /// Enable GPIO clock in RCC register (bits 0-7 control GPIOA-H, e.g.)
+ pub unsafe fn enable_gpio_clocks(rcc_ahb1enr_addr: u32, gpio_mask: u32) {
+     let enr = rcc_ahb1enr_addr as *mut u32;
+     write_volatile(enr, read_volatile(enr) | gpio_mask);
+ }
+ 
+ /// Configure pin as output (push-pull, high speed)
+ pub unsafe fn pin_to_output(port_base: u32, pin: u8) {
+     let moder = (port_base + MODER) as *mut u32;
+     let otyper = (port_base + OTYPER) as *mut u32;
+     let ospeedr = (port_base + OSPEEDR) as *mut u32;
+ 
+     let mut v = read_volatile(moder);
+     v &= !(0b11 << (pin * 2));
+     v |= 0b01 << (pin * 2); // output mode
+     write_volatile(moder, v);
+ 
+     let mut v = read_volatile(otyper);
+     v &= !(1 << pin); // push-pull output
+     write_volatile(otyper, v);
+ 
+     let mut v = read_volatile(ospeedr);
+     v &= !(0b11 << (pin * 2));
+     v |= 0b10 << (pin * 2); // high speed
+     write_volatile(ospeedr, v);
+ }
+ 
+ /// Configure pin as input with pull-up resistor
+ pub unsafe fn pin_to_input_pullup(port_base: u32, pin: u8) {
+     let moder = (port_base + MODER) as *mut u32;
+     let pupdr = (port_base + PUPDR) as *mut u32;
+ 
+     let mut v = read_volatile(moder);
+     v &= !(0b11 << (pin * 2)); // input mode (00)
+     write_volatile(moder, v);
+ 
+     let mut v = read_volatile(pupdr);
+     v &= !(0b11 << (pin * 2));
+     v |= 0b01 << (pin * 2); // pull-up (01)
+     write_volatile(pupdr, v);
+ }
+ 
+ /// Drive pin high or low using BSRR register (atomic)
+ pub unsafe fn drive_pin(port_base: u32, pin: u8, on: bool) {
+     let bsrr = (port_base + BSRR) as *mut u32;
+     if on {
+         write_volatile(bsrr, 1 << pin);
+     } else {
+         write_volatile(bsrr, 1 << (pin + 16));
+     }
+ }
+ 
+ /// Read input data register bit (true if pin is HIGH)
+ pub unsafe fn read_pin(port_base: u32, pin: u8) -> bool {
+     let idr = (port_base + IDR) as *const u32;
+     (read_volatile(idr) & (1 << pin)) != 0
+ }
+ 
+ /// Configure one pin for USART‑AF7 (UART/I²C/SPI share the same recipe)
+ pub unsafe fn pin_to_af7_usart(port_base: u32, pin: u8) {
+     const AFRL: u32 = 0x20; // AF register, pins 0‑7
+     // 1) MODER = 10 (alternate)
+     let moder = (port_base + MODER) as *mut u32;
+     let mut v = read_volatile(moder);
+     v &= !(0b11 << (pin * 2));
+     v |= 0b10 << (pin * 2);
+     write_volatile(moder, v);
+ 
+     // 2) AF[7] in AFRL
+     let afrl = (port_base + AFRL) as *mut u32;
+     let mut af = read_volatile(afrl);
+     af &= !(0xF << (pin * 4));
+     af |= 0x7 << (pin * 4); // AF7 = USART
+     write_volatile(afrl, af);
+ 
+     // 3) optional: push‑pull + very‑high speed
+     let otyper = (port_base + OTYPER) as *mut u32;
+     let ospeedr = (port_base + OSPEEDR) as *mut u32;
+     write_volatile(otyper, read_volatile(otyper) & !(1 << pin)); // PP
+     write_volatile(ospeedr, read_volatile(ospeedr) | 0b11 << (pin * 2)); // 100 MHz
+ }
+ 
+ // =============================================================================
+ // TIMER FUNCTIONALITY
+ // =============================================================================
+ 
+ // SysTick registers
+ const SYST_CSR: u32 = 0xE000_E010;
+ const SYST_RVR: u32 = 0xE000_E014;
+ const SYST_CVR: u32 = 0xE000_E018;
+ 
+ static mut SYSTEM_MS: u32 = 0;
+ 
+ /// Initialize SysTick timer for 1ms interrupts
+ pub unsafe fn systick_init(sysclk_hz: u32) {
+     let reload_value = (sysclk_hz / 1000) - 1; // 1ms period
+ 
+     // Disable SysTick first
+     write_volatile(SYST_CSR as *mut u32, 0);
+ 
+     // Set reload value
+     write_volatile(SYST_RVR as *mut u32, reload_value);
+ 
+     // Clear current value
+     write_volatile(SYST_CVR as *mut u32, 0);
+ 
+     // Enable SysTick with processor clock and interrupt
+     write_volatile(
+         SYST_CSR as *mut u32,
+         (1 << 0) |  // ENABLE
+         (1 << 1) |  // TICKINT - Enable interrupt
+         (1 << 2), // CLKSOURCE - Use processor clock
+     );
+ }
+ 
+ /// Get current system time in milliseconds
+ pub fn get_system_ms() -> u32 {
+     unsafe { SYSTEM_MS }
+ }
+ 
+ /// Simple delay function (busy wait)
+ pub fn delay_ms(ms: u32) {
+     let start = get_system_ms();
+     while get_system_ms().wrapping_sub(start) < ms {
+         asm::nop();
+     }
+ }
+ 
+ /// Delay with polling function called during wait
+ pub fn delay_ms_poll<F>(ms: u32, mut poll_fn: F)
+ where
+     F: FnMut(),
+ {
+     let start = get_system_ms();
+     while get_system_ms().wrapping_sub(start) < ms {
+         poll_fn();
+         asm::nop();
+     }
+ }
+ 
+ /// SysTick interrupt handler - must be registered in main.rs
+ /// Note: SysTick is a core exception, not a device interrupt
+ #[cortex_m_rt::exception]
+ fn SysTick() {
+     unsafe {
+         SYSTEM_MS = SYSTEM_MS.wrapping_add(1);
+     }
+ }
+ 
+ /// Get microsecond precision timing (approximate)
+ pub fn get_system_us() -> u32 {
+     unsafe {
+         let ms = SYSTEM_MS;
+         let current = read_volatile(SYST_CVR as *const u32);
+         let reload = read_volatile(SYST_RVR as *const u32);
+ 
+         // Calculate microseconds within current millisecond
+         // Note: SysTick counts down, so we need to invert
+         let us_in_ms = ((reload - current) * 1000) / (reload + 1);
+ 
+         ms * 1000 + us_in_ms
+     }
+ }
+ 
+ /// Reset system timer (useful for testing)
+ pub unsafe fn reset_system_time() {
+     SYSTEM_MS = 0;
+     write_volatile(SYST_CVR as *mut u32, 0);
+ }
+ 
+ /// Check if SysTick is enabled and running
+ pub fn is_systick_enabled() -> bool {
+     unsafe {
+         let csr = read_volatile(SYST_CSR as *const u32);
+         (csr & 1) != 0
+     }
+ }
+ 
+ /// Get the SysTick control and status register value
+ pub fn get_systick_csr() -> u32 {
+     unsafe { read_volatile(SYST_CSR as *const u32) }
+ }
+ 
+ // =============================================================================
+ // UART FUNCTIONALITY
+ // =============================================================================
+ 
+ /// A minimal ring buffer (power of two size).
+ pub struct Ring<const N: usize> {
+     buf: [u8; N],
+     head: usize,
+     tail: usize,
+ }
+ 
+ impl<const N: usize> Ring<N> {
+     pub const fn new() -> Self {
+         Self {
+             buf: [0; N],
+             head: 0,
+             tail: 0,
+         }
+     }
+ 
+     pub fn push(&mut self, b: u8) -> bool {
+         let next = (self.head + 1) & (N - 1);
+         if next == self.tail {
+             return false;
+         } // full
+         self.buf[self.head] = b;
+         self.head = next;
+         true
+     }
+ 
+     pub fn pop(&mut self) -> Option<u8> {
+         if self.head == self.tail {
+             return None;
+         }
+         let b = self.buf[self.tail];
+         self.tail = (self.tail + 1) & (N - 1);
+         Some(b)
+     }
+ 
+     pub fn is_empty(&self) -> bool {
+         self.head == self.tail
+     }
+ 
+     pub fn len(&self) -> usize {
+         (self.head.wrapping_sub(self.tail)) & (N - 1)
+     }
+ 
+     pub fn capacity(&self) -> usize {
+         N - 1 // One slot is always kept empty to distinguish full from empty
+     }
+ 
+     pub fn is_full(&self) -> bool {
+         ((self.head + 1) & (N - 1)) == self.tail
+     }
+ }
+ 
+ /// A very small driver for a single USART in **asynchronous 8-N-1**.
+ /// * `USARTx_BASE` is 0x4001_1000 for USART1, 0x4000_4400 for USART2, 0x4000_4800 for USART3, etc.
+ pub struct Uart<const USARTx_BASE: u32> {
+     pub tx_buf: Ring<256>,
+     pub rx_buf: Ring<256>,
+ }
+ 
+ impl<const B: u32> Uart<B> {
+     const SR: u32 = 0x00;
+     const DR: u32 = 0x04;
+     const BRR: u32 = 0x08;
+     const CR1: u32 = 0x0C;
+     const CR2: u32 = 0x10;
+     const CR3: u32 = 0x14;
+ 
+     pub const fn new() -> Self {
+         Self {
+             tx_buf: Ring::new(),
+             rx_buf: Ring::new(),
+         }
+     }
+ 
+     /// Enable clocks, set baud-rate, 8-N-1, RXNE + TXE interrupts.
+     pub unsafe fn init(&self, pclk_hz: u32, baud: u32, apb_enr_addr: *mut u32, enr_bit: u32) {
+         // 1) Enable clock
+         write_volatile(apb_enr_addr, read_volatile(apb_enr_addr) | enr_bit);
+ 
+         // 2) Disable USART before configuration
+         write_volatile((B + Self::CR1) as *mut u32, 0);
+ 
+         // 3) Set baud rate: BRR = pclk / baud
+         let brr = pclk_hz / baud;
+         write_volatile((B + Self::BRR) as *mut u32, brr);
+ 
+         // 4) Configure CR2 for 1 stop bit (default 00)
+         write_volatile((B + Self::CR2) as *mut u32, 0);
+ 
+         // 5) Configure CR3 (no hardware flow control)
+         write_volatile((B + Self::CR3) as *mut u32, 0);
+ 
+         // 6) Enable RXNEIE | TE | RE | UE (no TXEIE initially)
+         write_volatile(
+             (B + Self::CR1) as *mut u32,
+             (1 << 5)  // RXNEIE - RX not empty interrupt enable
+             | (1 << 3)  // TE - Transmitter enable  
+             | (1 << 2)  // RE - Receiver enable
+             | (1 << 13), // UE - USART enable
+         );
+     }
+ 
+     /// Called from main-line loop to push outbound data.
+     pub fn write_str(&mut self, s: &str) {
+         for b in s.bytes() {
+             self.tx_buf.push(b);
+         }
+         // Enable TXE interrupt to start transmission
+         unsafe {
+             let cr1 = (B + Self::CR1) as *mut u32;
+             write_volatile(cr1, read_volatile(cr1) | (1 << 7)); // TXEIE
+         }
+     }
+ 
+     /// Write a single byte
+     pub fn write_byte(&mut self, b: u8) {
+         self.tx_buf.push(b);
+         // Enable TXE interrupt to start transmission
+         unsafe {
+             let cr1 = (B + Self::CR1) as *mut u32;
+             write_volatile(cr1, read_volatile(cr1) | (1 << 7)); // TXEIE
+         }
+     }
+ 
+     pub fn try_read(&mut self) -> Option<u8> {
+         self.rx_buf.pop()
+     }
+ 
+     /// Check if transmit buffer is empty
+     pub fn tx_ready(&self) -> bool {
+         self.tx_buf.is_empty()
+     }
+ 
+     /// Check if receive buffer has data
+     pub fn rx_available(&self) -> bool {
+         !self.rx_buf.is_empty()
+     }
+ 
+     /// Interrupt handler **must** be registered in `#[interrupt]`
+     /// wrappers in main.rs.
+     pub unsafe fn isr(&mut self) {
+         let sr = read_volatile((B + Self::SR) as *const u32);
+ 
+         // Handle receive interrupt
+         if (sr & (1 << 5)) != 0 {
+             // RXNE - Receive data register not empty
+             let b = read_volatile((B + Self::DR) as *const u32) as u8;
+             self.rx_buf.push(b);
+         }
+ 
+         // Handle transmit interrupt
+         if (sr & (1 << 7)) != 0 {
+             // TXE - Transmit data register empty
+             if let Some(b) = self.tx_buf.pop() {
+                 write_volatile((B + Self::DR) as *mut u32, b as u32);
+             } else {
+                 // No more bytes: disable TXEIE
+                 let cr1 = (B + Self::CR1) as *mut u32;
+                 write_volatile(cr1, read_volatile(cr1) & !(1 << 7));
+             }
+         }
+ 
+         // Handle other potential interrupts/errors
+         if (sr & (1 << 3)) != 0 {
+             // ORE - Overrun error
+             // Clear by reading DR
+             let _ = read_volatile((B + Self::DR) as *const u32);
+         }
+ 
+         if (sr & (1 << 1)) != 0 {
+             // FE - Framing error
+             // Clear by reading DR
+             let _ = read_volatile((B + Self::DR) as *const u32);
+         }
+ 
+         if (sr & (1 << 2)) != 0 {
+             // NF - Noise detected flag
+             // Clear by reading DR
+             let _ = read_volatile((B + Self::DR) as *const u32);
+         }
+     }
+ 
+     /// Get the current status register value (for debugging)
+     pub unsafe fn get_status(&self) -> u32 {
+         read_volatile((B + Self::SR) as *const u32)
+     }
+ 
+     /// Clear all error flags
+     pub unsafe fn clear_errors(&self) {
+         // Reading DR clears ORE, FE, NF flags
+         let _ = read_volatile((B + Self::DR) as *const u32);
+     }
+ }
+ 
+ impl<const B: u32> core::fmt::Write for Uart<B> {
+     fn write_str(&mut self, s: &str) -> core::fmt::Result {
+         for b in s.bytes() {
+             self.tx_buf.push(b);
+         }
+         // Enable TXE interrupt to start transmission
+         unsafe {
+             let cr1 = (B + Self::CR1) as *mut u32;
+             write_volatile(cr1, read_volatile(cr1) | (1 << 7)); // TXEIE
+         }
+         Ok(())
+     }
+ }
+ 
+ // =============================================================================
+ // BUTTON FUNCTIONALITY
+ // =============================================================================
+ 
+ const DEBOUNCE_MS: u32 = 50;
+ 
+ #[derive(Copy, Clone)]
+ pub struct ButtonState {
+     pub is_pressed: bool,
+     pub last_change_ms: u32,
+ }
+ 
+ #[derive(PartialEq, Debug)]
+ pub enum ButtonEvent {
+     NoChange,
+     Pressed,
+     Released,
+ }
+ 
+ pub struct Buttons {
+     pub btn_a: ButtonState,
+     pub btn_b: ButtonState,
+     pub pin_a: u8,
+     pub pin_b: u8,
+     pub port_base: u32,
+ }
+ 
+ impl Buttons {
+     pub fn new(pin_a: u8, pin_b: u8, port_base: u32) -> Self {
+         Buttons {
+             btn_a: ButtonState {
+                 is_pressed: false,
+                 last_change_ms: 0,
+             },
+             btn_b: ButtonState {
+                 is_pressed: false,
+                 last_change_ms: 0,
+             },
+             pin_a,
+             pin_b,
+             port_base,
+         }
+     }
+ 
+     fn debounce(&mut self, raw: bool, st: &mut ButtonState, now: u32) -> ButtonEvent {
+         if now.wrapping_sub(st.last_change_ms) >= DEBOUNCE_MS {
+             if raw != st.is_pressed {
+                 st.is_pressed = raw;
+                 st.last_change_ms = now;
+                 if raw {
+                     return ButtonEvent::Pressed;
+                 } else {
+                     return ButtonEvent::Released;
+                 }
+             }
+         }
+         ButtonEvent::NoChange
+     }
+ 
+     pub fn poll(&mut self, now: u32) -> (ButtonEvent, ButtonEvent) {
+         let idr = unsafe { read_volatile((self.port_base + IDR) as *const u32) };
+         let raw_a = (idr & (1 << self.pin_a)) == 0;
+         let raw_b = (idr & (1 << self.pin_b)) == 0;
+ 
+         let mut event_a = ButtonEvent::NoChange;
+         let mut event_b = ButtonEvent::NoChange;
+ 
+         if now.wrapping_sub(self.btn_a.last_change_ms) >= DEBOUNCE_MS {
+             if raw_a != self.btn_a.is_pressed {
+                 self.btn_a.is_pressed = raw_a;
+                 self.btn_a.last_change_ms = now;
+                 event_a = if raw_a {
+                     ButtonEvent::Pressed
+                 } else {
+                     ButtonEvent::Released
+                 };
+             }
+         }
+ 
+         if now.wrapping_sub(self.btn_b.last_change_ms) >= DEBOUNCE_MS {
+             if raw_b != self.btn_b.is_pressed {
+                 self.btn_b.is_pressed = raw_b;
+                 self.btn_b.last_change_ms = now;
+                 event_b = if raw_b {
+                     ButtonEvent::Pressed
+                 } else {
+                     ButtonEvent::Released
+                 };
+             }
+         }
+ 
+         (event_a, event_b)
+     }
+ }
+ 
+ // =============================================================================
+ // TRAFFIC LIGHT FUNCTIONALITY
+ // =============================================================================
+ 
+ pub struct TrafficLights {
+     // Pins for road A
+     pub green_a: u8,
+     pub yellow_a: u8,
+     pub red_a: u8,
+ 
+     // Pins for road B
+     pub green_b: u8,
+     pub yellow_b: u8,
+     pub red_b: u8,
+ 
+     // Bar graph LEDs A
+     pub lvl1_a: u8,
+     pub lvl2_a: u8,
+     pub lvl3_a: u8,
+ 
+     // Bar graph LEDs B
+     pub lvl1_b: u8,
+     pub lvl2_b: u8,
+     pub lvl3_b: u8,
+ 
+     pub port_a: u32,
+     pub port_b: u32,
+ }
+ 
+ impl TrafficLights {
+     pub unsafe fn set_pair_a(&self, g: bool, y: bool, r: bool) {
+         drive_pin(self.port_a, self.green_a, g);
+         drive_pin(self.port_a, self.yellow_a, y);
+         drive_pin(self.port_a, self.red_a, r);
+     }
+     pub unsafe fn set_pair_b(&self, g: bool, y: bool, r: bool) {
+         drive_pin(self.port_b, self.green_b, g);
+         drive_pin(self.port_b, self.yellow_b, y);
+         drive_pin(self.port_b, self.red_b, r);
+     }
+     pub unsafe fn update_bargraphs(&self, level_a: u8, level_b: u8) {
+         drive_pin(self.port_a, self.lvl1_a, level_a >= 1);
+         drive_pin(self.port_a, self.lvl2_a, level_a >= 2);
+         drive_pin(self.port_a, self.lvl3_a, level_a >= 3);
+ 
+         drive_pin(self.port_b, self.lvl1_b, level_b >= 1);
+         drive_pin(self.port_b, self.lvl2_b, level_b >= 2);
+         drive_pin(self.port_b, self.lvl3_b, level_b >= 3);
+     }
+ }
+ 
+ #[cfg(test)]
+ mod tests {
+     use super::*;
+ 
+     #[test]
+     fn test_ring_buffer_basic() {
+         let mut ring: Ring<8> = Ring::new();
+ 
+         assert!(ring.is_empty());
+         assert!(!ring.is_full());
+         assert_eq!(ring.len(), 0);
+ 
+         // Push some data
+         assert!(ring.push(1));
+         assert!(ring.push(2));
+         assert!(ring.push(3));
+ 
+         assert!(!ring.is_empty());
+         assert_eq!(ring.len(), 3);
+ 
+         // Pop some data
+         assert_eq!(ring.pop(), Some(1));
+         assert_eq!(ring.pop(), Some(2));
+         assert_eq!(ring.len(), 1);
+ 
+         assert_eq!(ring.pop(), Some(3));
+         assert_eq!(ring.pop(), None);
+         assert!(ring.is_empty());
+     }
+ 
+     #[test]
+     fn test_ring_buffer_wrap_around() {
+         let mut ring: Ring<4> = Ring::new(); // Capacity is 3 (N-1)
+ 
+         // Fill to capacity
+         assert!(ring.push(1));
+         assert!(ring.push(2));
+         assert!(ring.push(3));
+         assert!(ring.is_full());
+         assert!(!ring.push(4)); // Should fail when full
+ 
+         // Pop one and push one
+         assert_eq!(ring.pop(), Some(1));
+         assert!(ring.push(4));
+         assert!(ring.is_full());
+ 
+         // Verify order
+         assert_eq!(ring.pop(), Some(2));
+         assert_eq!(ring.pop(), Some(3));
+         assert_eq!(ring.pop(), Some(4));
+         assert_eq!(ring.pop(), None);
+     }
+ }

+ #[derive(Copy, Clone)]
+ pub struct TLConfig {
+     pub g_ms: u32,
+     pub y_ms: u32,
+     pub r_ms: u32,
+     pub u_ms: u32, // light-traffic extension
+ }
+ 
+ impl TLConfig {
+     pub const fn new() -> Self {
+         Self {
+             g_ms: 10_000,
+             y_ms: 2_000,
+             r_ms: 10_000,
+             u_ms: 5_000,
+         }
+     }
+ }
+ 
+ #[derive(Copy, Clone)]
+ pub struct MonitorCfg {
+     pub interval_ms: u32,
+ }
+ 
+ impl MonitorCfg {
+     pub const fn new() -> Self {
+         Self {
+             interval_ms: 30_000,
+         }
+     }
+ }
+ 
+ #[derive(Copy, Clone)]
+ pub struct SystemConfig {
+     pub tl1: TLConfig,
+     pub tl2: TLConfig,
+     pub monitor: MonitorCfg,
+ }
+ 
+ impl SystemConfig {
+     pub const fn new() -> Self {
+         Self {
+             tl1: TLConfig::new(),
+             tl2: TLConfig::new(),
+             monitor: MonitorCfg::new(),
+         }
+     }
+ }
+ 
+ pub enum Cmd {
+     SetTL(u8, TLConfig), // traffic light x
+     SetMon(u32),         // monitor X
+     ReadTL(Option<u8>),  // read traffic light [x]
+     ReadMon,             // read traffic monitor
+     ReadAll,
+     Invalid,
+ }
+ 
+ /// Quick-n-dirty tokenizer; assumes ASCII & space-delimited.
+ pub fn parse(line: &str) -> Cmd {
+     let mut tok = line.split_ascii_whitespace();
+     match tok.next() {
+         Some("config") => match tok.next() {
+             Some("traffic") => match tok.next() {
+                 Some("light") => {
+                     let idx = tok.next().and_then(|s| s.parse::<u8>().ok()).unwrap_or(0);
+                     if idx == 0 || idx > 2 {
+                         return Cmd::Invalid;
+                     }
+ 
+                     // Skip the G Y R literals
+                     let _g = tok.next().unwrap_or("");
+                     let _y = tok.next().unwrap_or("");
+                     let _r = tok.next().unwrap_or("");
+ 
+                     // Parse the actual timing values
+                     let g = tok.next().and_then(|s| s.parse::<u32>().ok()).unwrap_or(0) * 1000;
+                     let y = tok.next().and_then(|s| s.parse::<u32>().ok()).unwrap_or(0) * 1000;
+                     let r = tok.next().and_then(|s| s.parse::<u32>().ok()).unwrap_or(0) * 1000;
+                     let u = tok.next().and_then(|s| s.parse::<u32>().ok()).unwrap_or(0) * 1000;
+ 
+                     if g == 0 || y == 0 || r == 0 {
+                         return Cmd::Invalid;
+                     }
+ 
+                     return Cmd::SetTL(
+                         idx,
+                         TLConfig {
+                             g_ms: g,
+                             y_ms: y,
+                             r_ms: r,
+                             u_ms: u,
+                         },
+                     );
+                 }
+                 Some("monitor") => {
+                     let x = tok.next().and_then(|s| s.parse::<u32>().ok()).unwrap_or(0);
+                     if x == 0 {
+                         return Cmd::Invalid;
+                     }
+                     return Cmd::SetMon(x * 1000);
+                 }
+                 _ => {}
+             },
+             _ => {}
+         },
+         Some("read") => match tok.next() {
+             None => return Cmd::ReadAll,
+             Some("traffic") => match tok.next() {
+                 Some("light") => {
+                     let idx = tok.next().and_then(|s| s.parse::<u8>().ok());
+                     if let Some(i) = idx {
+                         if i > 2 {
+                             return Cmd::Invalid;
+                         }
+                     }
+                     return Cmd::ReadTL(idx);
+                 }
+                 Some("monitor") => return Cmd::ReadMon,
+                 _ => {}
+             },
+             Some("all") => return Cmd::ReadAll,
+             _ => {}
+         },
+         _ => {}
+     };
+     Cmd::Invalid
+ }
+ 
+ /// Helpers that format current configuration or live status lines
+ pub fn format_cfg(cfg: &SystemConfig, tl: Option<u8>, out: &mut heapless::String<256>) {
+     match tl {
+         Some(1) => {
+             let _ = core::write!(
+                 out,
+                 "traffic light 1 G Y R {} {} {} {}\r\n",
+                 cfg.tl1.g_ms / 1000,
+                 cfg.tl1.y_ms / 1000,
+                 cfg.tl1.r_ms / 1000,
+                 cfg.tl1.u_ms / 1000
+             );
+         }
+         Some(2) => {
+             let _ = core::write!(
+                 out,
+                 "traffic light 2 G Y R {} {} {} {}\r\n",
+                 cfg.tl2.g_ms / 1000,
+                 cfg.tl2.y_ms / 1000,
+                 cfg.tl2.r_ms / 1000,
+                 cfg.tl2.u_ms / 1000
+             );
+         }
+         Some(_) => {
+             // Ignore invalid traffic light numbers
+         }
+         None => {
+             format_cfg(cfg, Some(1), out);
+             format_cfg(cfg, Some(2), out);
+             let _ = core::write!(
+                 out,
+                 "traffic monitor {}\r\n",
+                 cfg.monitor.interval_ms / 1000
+             );
+         }
+     }
+ }
+ 
+ // =============================================================================
+ // MAIN APPLICATION
+ // =============================================================================
  
  const RCC_AHB1ENR: u32 = 0x4002_3800 + 0x30;

Now I'll explain how the traffic management system works, focusing on the read/write operations at different levels:

## 📊 **Data Flow Architecture**

```
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│               INTERRUPT-DRIVEN DATA FLOW                   │
│                                                             │
│  Hardware Pins ←→ Registers ←→ Buffers ←→ Application      │
│                                                             │
│  [Physical]     [STM32 HW]    [Software]   [Logic]         │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

## 🔌 **GPIO Operations (Digital Pin Read/Write)**

### **Writing to Pins (Controlling LEDs/Traffic Lights)**

```rust
pub unsafe fn drive_pin(port_base: u32, pin: u8, on: bool) {
    let bsrr = (port_base + BSRR) as *mut u32;  // Bit Set Reset Register
    if on {
        write_volatile(bsrr, 1 << pin);         // Set bit (turn ON)
    } else {
        write_volatile(bsrr, 1 << (pin + 16));  // Reset bit (turn OFF)
    }
}
```

**How it works:**
- **BSRR Register**: Hardware register that atomically sets/resets pins
- **Bits 0-15**: Set pins (write 1 to turn ON)
- **Bits 16-31**: Reset pins (write 1 to turn OFF)
- **`write_volatile`**: Prevents compiler optimization, ensures hardware write happens

**Example Usage:**
```rust
// Turn on green light A (Pin 0 on GPIOA)
drive_pin(GPIOA_BASE, A_GREEN, true);   // Sets bit 0 in BSRR
// Turn off green light A  
drive_pin(GPIOA_BASE, A_GREEN, false);  // Sets bit 16 in BSRR
```

### **Reading from Pins (Button Input)**

```rust
pub unsafe fn read_pin(port_base: u32, pin: u8) -> bool {
    let idr = (port_base + IDR) as *const u32;    // Input Data Register
    (read_volatile(idr) & (1 << pin)) != 0       // Mask & check bit
}
```

**How it works:**
- **IDR Register**: Hardware register reflecting current pin states
- **Bit masking**: `(1 << pin)` creates mask for specific pin
- **`read_volatile`**: Ensures fresh read from hardware (not cached)

**Practical Example (Button Polling):**
```rust
pub fn poll(&mut self, now: u32) -> (ButtonEvent, ButtonEvent) {
    let idr = unsafe { read_volatile((self.port_base + IDR) as *const u32) };
    let raw_a = (idr & (1 << self.pin_a)) == 0;  // Button = LOW when pressed
    let raw_b = (idr & (1 << self.pin_b)) == 0;  // (pull-up resistor)
    
    // Debouncing logic prevents false triggers
    if now.wrapping_sub(self.btn_a.last_change_ms) >= DEBOUNCE_MS {
        if raw_a != self.btn_a.is_pressed {
            self.btn_a.is_pressed = raw_a;
            return ButtonEvent::Released;  // State change detected
        }
    }
}
```

## 📡 **UART Communication (Serial Read/Write)**

### **The Ring Buffer System**
```rust
pub struct Ring<const N: usize> {
    buf: [u8; N],       // Circular buffer
    head: usize,        // Write position  
    tail: usize,        // Read position
}
```

### **Writing Data (Sending)**

**Step 1: Application writes to buffer**
```rust
pub fn write_str(&mut self, s: &str) {
    for b in s.bytes() {
        self.tx_buf.push(b);        // Add to software buffer
    }
    // Enable interrupt to start hardware transmission
    let cr1 = (B + Self::CR1) as *mut u32;
    write_volatile(cr1, read_volatile(cr1) | (1 << 7)); // Set TXEIE bit
}
```

**Step 2: Interrupt handler sends data**
```rust
pub unsafe fn isr(&mut self) {
    let sr = read_volatile((B + Self::SR) as *const u32);  // Status register
    
    if (sr & (1 << 7)) != 0 {  // TXE - Transmit register empty
        if let Some(b) = self.tx_buf.pop() {               // Get next byte
            write_volatile((B + Self::DR) as *mut u32, b as u32); // Send to hardware
        } else {
            // Buffer empty - disable interrupt
            write_volatile(cr1, read_volatile(cr1) & !(1 << 7));
        }
    }
}
```

### **Reading Data (Receiving)**

**Step 1: Interrupt handler receives data**
```rust
if (sr & (1 << 5)) != 0 {  // RXNE - Receive register not empty
    let b = read_volatile((B + Self::DR) as *const u32) as u8;  // Read from hardware
    self.rx_buf.push(b);                                       // Store in buffer
}
```

**Step 2: Application processes data**
```rust
fn poll_serial(now: u32) {
    while let Some(b) = (*addr_of_mut!(UART2)).try_read() {  // Read from buffer
        match b {
            b'\r' | b'\n' => {  // Complete command received
                let cmd = parse(&*addr_of!(CMD_LINE));       // Parse command
                execute_cmd(cmd);                            // Execute action
            }
            b if b.is_ascii_graphic() => {
                CMD_LINE.push(b as char);                    // Build command
                UART2.write_byte(b);                        // Echo back
            }
        }
    }
}
```

## ⏰ **Timer Operations (SysTick)**

### **System Timing**
```rust
static mut SYSTEM_MS: u32 = 0;  // Global millisecond counter

#[cortex_m_rt::exception]
fn SysTick() {
    unsafe {
        SYSTEM_MS = SYSTEM_MS.wrapping_add(1);  // Increment every 1ms
    }
}

pub fn get_system_ms() -> u32 {
    unsafe { SYSTEM_MS }  // Thread-safe read
}
```

## 🚦 **Complete Traffic Control Flow**

### **Input → Processing → Output Chain**

```rust
// 1. READ: Button input changes traffic level
let (evt_a, evt_b) = buttons.poll(now);
if evt_a == ButtonEvent::Released {
    (*addr_of_mut!(TRAFFIC)).level_a = ((*addr_of!(TRAFFIC)).level_a + 1) % 4;
}

// 2. PROCESS: State machine determines light pattern  
match (*addr_of!(TRAFFIC)).state {
    TrafficPhase::AGreenBRed => {
        set_lights(&traffic_lights, true, false, false, false, false, true);
        if elapsed >= green_time_ms(level_a) {  // Time-based transitions
            (*addr_of_mut!(TRAFFIC)).state = TrafficPhase::AYellowBRed;
        }
    }
}

// 3. WRITE: Update physical lights
pub unsafe fn set_pair_a(&self, g: bool, y: bool, r: bool) {
    drive_pin(self.port_a, self.green_a, g);   // GPIO write operations
    drive_pin(self.port_a, self.yellow_a, y);
    drive_pin(self.port_a, self.red_a, r);
}
```

## 🔄 **Interrupt-Driven Architecture**

```
Timer Interrupt (1ms)     UART Interrupts (async)      Main Loop (continuous)
       ↓                         ↓                            ↓
   Update SYSTEM_MS          RX: Data → Buffer            Poll buttons
                            TX: Buffer → Hardware        Update traffic FSM  
                                                         Process commands
                                                         Update outputs
```

## 🎯 **Key Design Patterns**

1. **Volatile Operations**: All hardware access uses `read_volatile`/`write_volatile` to prevent optimization
2. **Ring Buffers**: Decouple interrupt timing from application processing
3. **State Machines**: Deterministic traffic light control
4. **Debouncing**: Prevents button noise from causing false triggers
5. **Interrupt Safety**: Critical sections protected with `unsafe` blocks

The system elegantly separates **hardware abstraction** (registers, interrupts) from **application logic** (traffic control, command processing), enabling robust real-time operation on embedded hardware.

#### **🔌 `enable_gpio_clocks(rcc_ahb1enr_addr, gpio_mask)`**
**Purpose**: Enable power to GPIO ports (A, B, C) so they can operate
```rust
pub unsafe fn enable_gpio_clocks(rcc_ahb1enr_addr: u32, gpio_mask: u32) {
    let enr = rcc_ahb1enr_addr as *mut u32;  // RCC Enable Register
    write_volatile(enr, read_volatile(enr) | gpio_mask);  // Set clock bits
}
```
- **Called**: Once during initialization 
- **Input**: `gpio_mask = (1<<0)|(1<<1)|(1<<2)` enables GPIOA, GPIOB, GPIOC
- **Effect**: Powers up GPIO hardware blocks

#### **📤 `pin_to_output(port_base, pin)`**
**Purpose**: Configure a specific pin as an output (for LEDs/traffic lights)
```rust
pub unsafe fn pin_to_output(port_base: u32, pin: u8) {
    // MODER: Set pin to output mode (01)
    let mut v = read_volatile(moder);
    v &= !(0b11 << (pin * 2));      // Clear 2 bits
    v |= 0b01 << (pin * 2);         // Set to output mode
    write_volatile(moder, v);
    
    // OTYPER: Set to push-pull (not open-drain)
    v &= !(1 << pin);               // Clear bit = push-pull
    
    // OSPEEDR: Set to high speed
    v |= 0b10 << (pin * 2);         // High speed output
}
```
- **Called**: For each LED pin during initialization (12 pins total)
- **Effect**: Pin can now drive LEDs ON/OFF

#### **📥 `pin_to_input_pullup(port_base, pin)`**
**Purpose**: Configure pin as input with internal pull-up resistor (for buttons)
```rust
pub unsafe fn pin_to_input_pullup(port_base: u32, pin: u8) {
    // MODER: Set to input mode (00)
    v &= !(0b11 << (pin * 2));      // Clear = input mode
    
    // PUPDR: Enable pull-up resistor (01)  
    v |= 0b01 << (pin * 2);         // Pull-up enabled
}
```
- **Called**: For button pins (BTN_A_PIN, BTN_B_PIN)
- **Effect**: Button reads HIGH when not pressed, LOW when pressed

#### **⏰ `systick_init(sysclk_hz)`** - **SYSTEM HEARTBEAT**
**Purpose**: Initialize 1ms system timer for precise timing
```rust
pub unsafe fn systick_init(sysclk_hz: u32) {
    let reload_value = (sysclk_hz / 1000) - 1;  // 16MHz ÷ 1000 = 16000 ticks/ms
    
    write_volatile(SYST_RVR as *mut u32, reload_value);  // Set reload value
    write_volatile(SYST_CSR as *mut u32, 
        (1 << 0) |   // ENABLE - Start counting
        (1 << 1) |   // TICKINT - Generate interrupt every 1ms
        (1 << 2)     // CLKSOURCE - Use processor clock
    );
}
```
- **Called**: Once during initialization
- **Effect**: Generates interrupt every 1ms → updates `SYSTEM_MS`

**Purpose**: Get current system time in milliseconds

#### **⏳ `delay_ms(ms)`** 
**Purpose**: Block execution for specified milliseconds
```rust
pub fn delay_ms(ms: u32) {
    let start = get_system_ms();
    while get_system_ms().wrapping_sub(start) < ms {
        asm::nop();  // Prevent optimization, keep CPU busy
    }
}
```
- **Called**: At end of main loop (`delay_ms(1)`) to prevent CPU overload

#### **🔔 `SysTick()` - INTERRUPT HANDLER**
**Purpose**: Increment system time counter every 1ms
```rust
#[cortex_m_rt::exception]
fn SysTick() {
    unsafe {
        SYSTEM_MS = SYSTEM_MS.wrapping_add(1);  // Atomic increment
    }
}
```
- **Called**: Automatically by hardware every 1ms
- **Effect**: Updates global time reference

#### **📦 `Ring<N>` - CIRCULAR BUFFER**
**Purpose**: Thread-safe buffer for UART data (256 bytes each for TX/RX)
```rust
pub fn push(&mut self, b: u8) -> bool {
    let next = (self.head + 1) & (N - 1);  // Wrap around using mask
    if next == self.tail { return false; } // Buffer full
    self.buf[self.head] = b;
    self.head = next;
    true
}

pub fn pop(&mut self) -> Option<u8> {
    if self.head == self.tail { return None; }  // Buffer empty
    let b = self.buf[self.tail];
    self.tail = (self.tail + 1) & (N - 1);      // Wrap around
    Some(b)
}
```
- **Used by**: All UART instances for buffering TX/RX data
- **Thread-safe**: Interrupt can write while main loop reads

#### **🔧 `Uart::init(pclk_hz, baud, apb_enr_addr, enr_bit)`**
**Purpose**: Configure UART hardware for 115200 baud, 8-N-1 format
```rust
pub unsafe fn init(&self, pclk_hz: u32, baud: u32, apb_enr_addr: *mut u32, enr_bit: u32) {
    // 1. Enable UART clock in RCC
    write_volatile(apb_enr_addr, read_volatile(apb_enr_addr) | enr_bit);
    
    // 2. Calculate and set baud rate  
    let brr = pclk_hz / baud;  // 16MHz ÷ 115200 = 139
    write_volatile((B + Self::BRR) as *mut u32, brr);
    
    // 3. Enable: RX interrupt, Transmitter, Receiver, UART
    write_volatile((B + Self::CR1) as *mut u32,
        (1 << 5)  |  // RXNEIE - RX interrupt
        (1 << 3)  |  // TE - Transmit enable
        (1 << 2)  |  // RE - Receive enable  
        (1 << 13)    // UE - UART enable
    );
}
```
- **Called**: For all 3 UARTs during initialization
- **Result**: UART ready for communication

#### **📤 `write_str(s)` & `write_byte(b)`** - **SEND DATA**
**Purpose**: Queue data for transmission via UART
```rust
pub fn write_str(&mut self, s: &str) {
    for b in s.bytes() {
        self.tx_buf.push(b);  // Add to software buffer
    }
    // Enable TXE interrupt to start hardware transmission
    let cr1 = (B + Self::CR1) as *mut u32;
    write_volatile(cr1, read_volatile(cr1) | (1 << 7)); // Set TXEIE bit
}
```
- **Called**: For sending commands, status reports, responses
- **Non-blocking**: Returns immediately, interrupt handles actual transmission

#### **📥 `try_read()` → Option<u8>`** - **RECEIVE DATA**
**Purpose**: Get next received byte from buffer
```rust
pub fn try_read(&mut self) -> Option<u8> {
    self.rx_buf.pop()  // Returns Some(byte) or None if empty
}
```
- **Called**: In main loop to process incoming commands
- **Non-blocking**: Returns None if no data available

#### **🔔 `isr()` - UART INTERRUPT HANDLER** - **CRITICAL**
**Purpose**: Handle UART receive/transmit interrupts (called automatically by hardware)
```rust
pub unsafe fn isr(&mut self) {
    let sr = read_volatile((B + Self::SR) as *const u32);  // Read status
    
    // RECEIVE: New data arrived
    if (sr & (1 << 5)) != 0 {  // RXNE bit
        let b = read_volatile((B + Self::DR) as *const u32) as u8;
        self.rx_buf.push(b);   // Store in buffer
    }
    
    // TRANSMIT: Hardware ready for next byte
    if (sr & (1 << 7)) != 0 {  // TXE bit
        if let Some(b) = self.tx_buf.pop() {
            write_volatile((B + Self::DR) as *mut u32, b as u32);  // Send byte
        } else {
            // Buffer empty - disable TX interrupt
            write_volatile(cr1, read_volatile(cr1) & !(1 << 7));
        }
    }
}
```
- **Called**: Automatically when UART events occur
- **Effect**: Transfers data between hardware and software buffers

#### **🔍 `poll(now)` → (ButtonEvent, ButtonEvent)** - **INPUT PROCESSOR**
**Purpose**: Check button states and detect press/release events with debouncing
```rust
pub fn poll(&mut self, now: u32) -> (ButtonEvent, ButtonEvent) {
    // Read hardware pins
    let idr = unsafe { read_volatile((self.port_base + IDR) as *const u32) };
    let raw_a = (idr & (1 << self.pin_a)) == 0;  // LOW = pressed (pull-up)
    let raw_b = (idr & (1 << self.pin_b)) == 0;
    
    // Debounce logic (50ms minimum between changes)
    if now.wrapping_sub(self.btn_a.last_change_ms) >= DEBOUNCE_MS {
        if raw_a != self.btn_a.is_pressed {
            self.btn_a.is_pressed = raw_a;
            self.btn_a.last_change_ms = now;
            event_a = if raw_a { ButtonEvent::Pressed } else { ButtonEvent::Released };
        }
    }
    
    return (event_a, event_b);
}
```
- **Called**: Every main loop iteration (~1000Hz)
- **Returns**: Events only when button state actually changes
- **Prevents**: Button noise from causing false triggers

#### **📝 `parse(line)` → Cmd** - **COMMAND INTERPRETER**
**Purpose**: Parse text commands received via UART into structured commands
```rust
pub fn parse(line: &str) -> Cmd {
    let mut tok = line.split_ascii_whitespace();
    match tok.next() {
        Some("config") => match tok.next() {
            Some("traffic") => match tok.next() {
                Some("light") => {
                    // "config traffic light 1 G Y R 8 2 8 4"
                    let idx = tok.next().parse::<u8>()?;        // "1" → 1
                    let _g = tok.next();  // Skip "G"
                    let _y = tok.next();  // Skip "Y" 
                    let _r = tok.next();  // Skip "R"
                    let g = tok.next().parse::<u32>()? * 1000;  // "8" → 8000ms
                    let y = tok.next().parse::<u32>()? * 1000;  // "2" → 2000ms
                    let r = tok.next().parse::<u32>()? * 1000;  // "8" → 8000ms
                    let u = tok.next().parse::<u32>()? * 1000;  // "4" → 4000ms
                    
                    return Cmd::SetTL(idx, TLConfig { g_ms: g, y_ms: y, r_ms: r, u_ms: u });
                }
            }
        }
        Some("read") => /* ... parse read commands ... */
    }
}
```
- **Called**: When complete command line received via UART
- **Supports**: Configuration commands, read commands, monitoring settings

#### **⚙️ `execute_cmd(cmd)`** - **COMMAND EXECUTOR**
**Purpose**: Execute parsed commands and update system configuration
```rust
fn execute_cmd(cmd: Cmd) {
    match cmd {
        Cmd::SetTL(idx, new_cfg) => {
            // Update traffic light timing configuration
            match idx {
                1 => (*addr_of_mut!(CFG)).tl1 = new_cfg,  // Traffic Light 1
                2 => (*addr_of_mut!(CFG)).tl2 = new_cfg,  // Traffic Light 2
            }
            UART2.write_str("OK\r\n");  // Acknowledge
            
            // Forward to upstream controller
            let cmd_str = format!("config traffic light {} G Y R {} {} {} {}\r\n", 
                                  idx, new_cfg.g_ms/1000, new_cfg.y_ms/1000, 
                                  new_cfg.r_ms/1000, new_cfg.u_ms/1000);
            UARTA.write_str(&cmd_str);
        }
        
        Cmd::ReadAll => {
            // Send current configuration back to user
            let mut buf = heapless::String<256>::new();
            format_cfg(&CFG, None, &mut buf);
            UART2.write_str(&buf);
        }
    }
}
```
- **Called**: After successful command parsing
- **Actions**: Updates configuration, sends responses, forwards to upstream

#### **⏱️ `green_time_ms(level)` → u32** - **ADAPTIVE TIMING**
**Purpose**: Calculate green light duration based on traffic level (0-3)
```rust
fn green_time_ms(level: u8) -> u32 {
    match level {
        0 => CFG.tl1.g_ms,                           // Base: 10s
        1 => CFG.tl1.g_ms + CFG.tl1.u_ms / 3,       // +1.67s = 11.67s
        2 => CFG.tl1.g_ms + (CFG.tl1.u_ms * 2) / 3, // +3.33s = 13.33s  
        3 => CFG.tl1.g_ms + CFG.tl1.u_ms,           // +5s = 15s
        _ => CFG.tl1.g_ms,
    }
}
```
- **Called**: By traffic state machine to determine phase timing
- **Logic**: Higher traffic level = longer green time
- **Range**: 10s (level 0) to 15s (level 3)

#### **🚦 Traffic State Machine** - **CORE CONTROL LOGIC**
**Purpose**: Control traffic light sequence with adaptive timing
```rust
// State machine runs every main loop iteration (~1000Hz)
let elapsed = now.wrapping_sub(TRAFFIC.phase_start_ms);

match TRAFFIC.state {
    TrafficPhase::AGreenBRed => {
        set_lights(&traffic_lights, true, false, false, false, false, true);
        //                          A_G   A_Y   A_R   B_G   B_Y   B_R
        if elapsed >= green_time_ms(TRAFFIC.level_a) {  // Adaptive timing
            TRAFFIC.state = TrafficPhase::AYellowBRed;
            next_phase = true;
        }
    }
    TrafficPhase::AYellowBRed => {
        set_lights(&traffic_lights, false, true, false, false, false, true);
        if elapsed >= CFG.tl1.y_ms {  // Fixed yellow time (2s)
            TRAFFIC.state = TrafficPhase::ARedBGreen;
            next_phase = true;
        }
    }
    /* ... similar for other phases ... */
}
```

**State Sequence:**
1. **A Green, B Red** → Duration based on traffic level A
2. **A Yellow, B Red** → Fixed 2 seconds  
3. **A Red, B Green** → Duration based on traffic level B
4. **A Red, B Yellow** → Fixed 2 seconds
5. **Repeat cycle**

#### **📊 `send_status_report(now)`** - **MONITORING OUTPUT**
**Purpose**: Send periodic status reports to PC console with color coding
```rust
fn send_status_report(now: u32) {
    let ts = now / 1000;  // Convert to seconds
    let uart = &mut UART2;
    
    // Line 1: Traffic Light 1 (EW) status with colors
    uart.write_str(ANSI_CYAN);
    write!(uart, "{} traffic light 1 (EW)  ", ts).ok();
    
    uart.write_str(if LED_STATE_A_GREEN { ANSI_GREEN } else { ANSI_RED });
    uart.write_str(if LED_STATE_A_GREEN { "ON " } else { "OFF " });
    
    uart.write_str(if LED_STATE_A_YELLOW { ANSI_GREEN } else { ANSI_RED });
    uart.write_str(if LED_STATE_A_YELLOW { "ON " } else { "OFF " });
    
    uart.write_str(if LED_STATE_A_RED { ANSI_GREEN } else { ANSI_RED });
    uart.write_str(if LED_STATE_A_RED { "ON" } else { "OFF" });
    
    // Lines 2-5: Similar for Traffic Light 2, levels, directions...
}
```
- **Called**: Every 30 seconds (configurable via `monitor.interval_ms`)
- **Output**: Timestamp, light states, traffic levels, traffic conditions
- **Colors**: Green=ON, Red=OFF for easy visual parsing

loop {
    let now = get_system_ms();  // Get current timestamp

    let (evt_a, evt_b) = buttons.poll(now);
    if evt_a == ButtonEvent::Released {
        TRAFFIC.level_a = (TRAFFIC.level_a + 1) % 4;  // Cycle 0→1→2→3→0

    poll_serial(now);  // Process UART commands
    
    // 3. TRAFFIC CONTROL
    // Run state machine (shown above)
    
    // 4. CPU THROTTLING
    delay_ms(1);  // Prevent 100% CPU usage
}

# 🌊 **COMPLETE SYSTEM WORKFLOW**

## **🔄 Execution Flow Diagram**

```
STARTUP SEQUENCE:
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│ 1. enable_gpio_clocks() → Power up GPIO blocks                 │
│ 2. pin_to_output() × 12 → Configure LED pins                   │
│ 3. pin_to_input_pullup() × 2 → Configure button pins          │
│ 4. systick_init() → Start 1ms timer                           │  
│ 5. pin_to_af7_usart() × 2 → Configure UART pins              │
│ 6. uart.init() × 3 → Configure UARTs                          │
│ 7. NVIC::unmask() × 3 → Enable UART interrupts               │
│ 8. Ready message sent → System operational                     │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

RUNTIME LOOP (1000Hz):
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│ 1. get_system_ms() → Get timestamp                            │
│ 2. buttons.poll() → Check for button events                   │
│ 3. If button released: update level + update_bargraphs()      │
│ 4. poll_serial() → Process UART data                          │
│    ├─ try_read() → Get received bytes                         │
│    ├─ Parse commands when \r\n received                       │
│    ├─ execute_cmd() → Update configuration                    │
│    └─ Send responses                                           │
│ 5. Traffic State Machine:                                     │
│    ├─ Calculate elapsed time                                   │
│    ├─ set_lights() → Update physical LEDs                     │
│    └─ Change state when time expires                          │
│ 6. Periodic: send_status_report() every 30s                   │
│ 7. delay_ms(1) → CPU throttling                              │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

INTERRUPT HANDLERS (Asynchronous):
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│ SysTick() → SYSTEM_MS++ every 1ms                             │
│ USART1/2/3() → UART data transfer via uart.isr()             │
│    ├─ RX: Hardware → rx_buf (when data arrives)              │
│    └─ TX: tx_buf → Hardware (when ready)                     │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

## **🎯 Key Function Interaction Patterns**

### **Data Flow: Button → Traffic Control**
```
Button Press → buttons.poll() → ButtonEvent::Released → 
level_a++ → update_bargraphs() → drive_pin() → LED ON
```

### **Data Flow: UART Command → Configuration**
```
UART RX → uart.isr() → rx_buf.push() → poll_serial() → 
try_read() → parse() → execute_cmd() → CFG update → 
write_str() → tx_buf.push() → uart.isr() → UART TX
```

### **Data Flow: Traffic State Machine**
```
get_system_ms() → elapsed calculation → green_time_ms() → 
state transition → set_lights() → set_pair_a/b() → 
drive_pin() → Physical LEDs
```

The system elegantly combines **hardware abstraction** (register-level operations), **real-time control** (interrupt-driven timing), and **application logic** (traffic management) into a cohesive, safety-critical embedded system. Every function has a specific role in maintaining smooth, adaptive traffic flow while providing comprehensive monitoring and remote configuration capabilities.
